WI-03 (UC-009) — Extend the 50k perf seeder with full analytics shapes.

IMPLEMENTATION SUMMARY:

1. SUPPORTING ROWS (seeded before orders to satisfy FK constraints):
   - 1 Dispatcher user (actor for Assigned order_events; must be a real user row per CLAUDE.md)
   - 5 Driver users + 5 Driver profile rows (orders.driver_id -> drivers.id FK)
   - 5 Vehicle rows (driver_shifts.vehicle_id FK; orders.vehicle_id FK)
   - 10 Customer user rows (orders.customer_user_id -> users.id FK)
   All rows use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING for idempotency within a fleet.

2. DRIVER SHIFTS: set-based INSERT...SELECT FROM generate_series(0,59) CROSS JOIN VALUES clause with 5 driver/vehicle pairs. ~300 shifts total per fleet (5 drivers x ~60 shifts over 180 days). Hour jitter via modulo arithmetic prevents all shifts landing in the same time bucket.

3. STATUS DISTRIBUTION (20-bucket cycle via gs % 20):
   - 0-11 (60%): Completed with driver, vehicle, full lifecycle timestamps
   - 12-14 (15%): Cancelled while New (no driver, no AssignedAt)
   - 15-16 (10%): Cancelled while Assigned (driver offered, no accept, cancelled_by_role='Dispatcher')
   - 17 (5%): No-show (driver arrived, cancelled_by_role='Driver')
   - 18-19 (10%): Offer funnel path, ends Completed

4. CUSTOMER IDENTITY MIX (gs % 10):
   - 0 (10%): anonymized, phone='+420000000000'
   - 1-3 (30%): returning customer, customer_user_id set to pool of 10 real user rows
   - 4-9 (60%): one-timer, distinct phone, no customer_user_id

5. RATINGS: ~30% of completed orders get rating_stars (1-5 spread via gs % 5). ~50% of rated orders get a rating_comment string + rated_at timestamp.

6. TIMESTAMPS: created_at spread across 180 days with hour jitter: (gs * 7 % 24) hours + (gs * 13 % 60) minutes. This produces 24 distinct hour values across 500+ orders.

7. ORDER EVENTS: Single UNION-ALL INSERT covering all event types:
   - Assigned (actor=dispatcher, every order with assigned_at)
   - Accepted (actor=driver user, every order with accepted_at)
   - Completed (actor=driver user, every completed order)
   - Cancelled (actor=null for Customer cancels, dispatcher for Dispatcher cancels)
   - Declined (actor=driver user, Cancelled-while-Assigned subset)
   - Timeout (actor_user_id=NULL/System, Cancelled-while-Assigned subset)

8. FK CORRECTNESS: All actor_user_id values are real user rows (dispatcher or driver user IDs). Timeout events use NULL actor_user_id (System). driver_user_map CTE joins driver_id -> user_id for correct actor resolution.

9. EF1002 SUPPRESSION: Three pragma disable/restore EF1002 regions around the three interpolated SQL strings (shift VALUES, order pool CTEs, event driver_user_map CTE). The interpolated values are exclusively server-generated GUIDs.

10. IDEMPOTENCY: The existing 'if (existing) return;' guard is preserved. All subsidiary INSERT statements use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

- GREEN: Full implementation added. First iteration still failed on hasTimeoutEvent (half-filter modulo was unreliable). Fixed: removed the epoch%2 half-filter, all Cancelled-while-Assigned rows get Timeout events.
- All 11 assertions pass.

SEED RUNTIME: ~800ms for 500 orders (test-scale). 50k scale not measured in this session (opt-in perf test).

NOTE: driver_shifts.vehicle_id FK requires vehicle rows. The seeder creates 5 vehicles for this. The existing perf test (FleetReport_50kOrders_RespondsUnder300ms) is opt-in (RUN_PERF_TESTS=1) and distributes orders across all status buckets at 50k scale.
